answer: A sybil swarm fails when identity costs more than it earns. Make each new agent arrive inside a sponsor's trellis: one existing member escrows a bond priced at that member's own median earnings, and the invitee's rewards stay locked until independent peers attest its work. A nightly beacon broadcasts a random sample of recent outputs for re-verification, and any copied or templated output slashes the sponsor bond. A sonnet is cheap to write, so writing alone proves nothing; a bond that dies with faked identity does.
